inline_comments.comment: The Angular framework's `.storybook/tsconfig.json` templates hardcode `"./preview.ts"` in their `include` array (see `code/lib/create-storybook/templates/angular/application/template-csf/.storybook/tsconfig.json` and the library variant). Those template files are not updated in this PR. As a result, newly initialized Angular projects will have a `preview.tsx` file (generated here) that TypeScript's language server cannot find or type-check, because the generated tsconfig still includes only `"./preview.ts"`. TypeScript will silently skip type-checking the preview file. The templates need to be updated to `"./preview.tsx"` (or a broader glob like `"./preview.*"`) in lockstep with this change.

The mechanical replacement turns `preview.js|jsx` into `preview.jsx|jsx` and `preview.ts|tsx` into `preview.tsx|tsx`. The pipe notation was a documentation convention meaning "the file can be named with either extension"; `preview.js|jsx` meant ".js or .jsx". After the substitution, `preview.jsx|jsx` means ".jsx or .jsx" — which is redundant and meaningless. These entries should be simplified to `preview.jsx` and `preview.tsx` respectively (without the pipe). The same pattern recurs for the CSF Next variants a few lines further down in the same file.

This snippet documents an *addon author's* internal preview file (`example-addon/src/preview.js`), not a user's `.storybook/preview` file. Renaming it to `preview.jsx`/`preview.tsx` goes beyond this PR's stated scope and unnecessarily prescribes JSX-capable extensions for addon previews that may target Angular, Vue, Svelte, or web-components renderers where JSX is not used. Leave addon source file examples as `.ts`/`.js` unless they actually contain JSX.

general_comments.comment: The Angular `.storybook/tsconfig.json` templates (`code/lib/create-storybook/templates/angular/application/template-csf/.storybook/tsconfig.json` and the library equivalent) hardcode `"include": ["../src/**/*.stories.*", "./preview.ts"]`. Because those files are not updated in this PR, every newly scaffolded Angular project will have a mismatch: the generator emits `preview.tsx`, but the tsconfig include list only covers `preview.ts`. TypeScript will not find or check the preview file in Angular projects created after this change. This should be treated as a blocking omission — the template files must be updated (or the include glob broadened to `./preview.*`) before merging.

Across the updated documentation, references to `main.js|ts` are left unchanged (since `main` is not getting a JSX extension) while `preview.js|ts` is now `preview.jsx|tsx`. This creates an inconsistent notation style in the same sentences — e.g., "upgrade your `.storybook/main.js|ts` and `.storybook/preview.jsx|tsx` files." Readers unfamiliar with the rationale may find the asymmetry confusing. A short inline note in key places (e.g., in `AGENTS.md` or the configure story-rendering page) explaining why `preview` uses `jsx`/`tsx` while `main` does not would eliminate that confusion.
